records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb members has no upper bound on params[:limit], letting an unauthenticated request pass ?limit=1000000 and force full serialization of every group user
records.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)` with no maximum cap or validation. A client can pass an arbitrarily large `?limit=` and cause serialization of the entire group membership (up to total users), which is a performance/DoS risk. The diff does not show any upper-bound enforcement.

records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb members passes params[:offset].to_i straight to .offset(), so a negative offset makes PostgreSQL raise 'OFFSET must not be negative' and return a 500
records.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then calls `group.users...offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. A request like `?offset=-1` would pass `-1` through to ActiveRecord/PostgreSQL, which can raise an error (e.g., "OFFSET must not be negative") and result in a 500.

records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb add_members calls params.require(:usernames).split(','), which raises NoMethodError (500 instead of 400) when a client posts usernames as an array
records.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",")`. If a client submits `usernames` as an Array (e.g., `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` or JSON array), `split` is undefined on Array and will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. The diff shows no guarding/coercion for non-String inputs.
